EDITORIAL INTRODUCTION

Beneath the battlefield.

The Crimson Siege is built around two wars happening at once: the visible slaughter above and the older, stranger contest beneath the fortress. The story's battlefield is huge, but its real pressure comes from the hidden wizards who can alter the war without ever stepping into it.

FEATURED PASSAGE
Above the world, war howls like a rabid beast. A hellish battlefield stretches endlessly, soaked in blood and ash.

The opening sells scale immediately, then the story pulls downward into the underground chambers where incense, runes, relics and summoning become the machinery behind the violence above.

EDITORIAL NOTE

Rituals below. Blood above.

One of the strongest ideas in the piece is that the wizards are not clean allies or obvious villains. They summon horrors, influence both sides and continue their work whether the kingdom wins or loses. That ambiguity makes the war feel larger than the soldiers experiencing it.

REALM CONNECTION

A window into the Realms.

The story functions as one archive window into a broader world of warriors, sorcerers, dragons, demons, artifacts and forces that may intersect across later Grim Sagas entries. The post-story note and Keeper of the Core teaser make that larger-world intention explicit.
